source_caption_text:
⬇️ TODAY IN HIP-HOP ⬇️

2024: After spending 906 days in jail fighting a RICO case in Atlanta, Young Thug strikes a deal in the middle of the trial and is released from custody.

Young Thug, Gunna and 26 other affiliates of YSL were originally charged and arrested on May 9, 2022. The lengthy indictment claimed YSL was a violent street gang that committed multiple crimes in the Atlanta area, including murder, robbery, assaults and shootings for a decade.

Several of the people charged took plea deals, including Gunna, who was released on Dec. 14, 2022.

The trial, which ended up being the longest trial in Georgia history, began on Nov. 27, 2023, with six defendants. In a twist, on Oct. 31, 2024, Thug pleaded guilty to charges of participating in a criminal street gang, violation of Georgia’s controlled substance act and multiple gun crimes. He was sentenced to 40 years, with five years to service, but commuted to time served with 15 years of probation followed by backloaded 20 years.

During his plea hearing, Thug apologized for his crimes.

“I take full responsibility for, you know, my crimes or my charges,” he said. “I want to say sorry to my family, my mom. My mom got 11 kids. I can’t say all their names, you know, my managers, my kids that’s not here. Really everybody that got something to do with this situation, I want to say sorry for just like, you know, being, having so much time investing into this, you know. I am a smart guy. I’m a good guy and I really got a good heart, you know?”
